messages:

Subject: Helion Health — initial compromise proposal on IP indemnity / evidence

Lara / Tom,

Thanks for the detailed redlines. We reviewed Helion's markups and discussed trade-offs with Sales and Legal. To keep momentum on the deal while addressing Helion's concerns, here's a proposed middle-path we can offer:

1) Scope: Redwood will indemnify and defend third-party IP infringement claims that directly arise from the Model outputs delivered to Helion under the MSA/Order Form, subject to the limitations below. This stays limited to third-party claims (no broad customer-origin liability).

2) Defense/control: Redwood will take primary defense rights for covered claims but will allow Helion reasonable participation (outside counsel approval rights for settlement that admits liability or imposes material obligations).

3) Limit & cap: Aggregate cap for Redwood indemnity tied to the Order Form value or 12 months of fees (whichever is greater). We are not able to accept uncapped exposure.

4) Proof-of-origin / evidence burden: Redwood will cooperate to produce evidence reasonably available in our systems to evaluate a claim (model snapshot, input/trace logs, limited training provenance notes where applicable). To be practical and protect customer data/ops, that will be limited to: (a) logged request/response payloads for the time window in question, (b) model version hash and deployment config, (c) training-source metadata at a high level (not full dataset exports). We propose an explicit timeline: Redwood will acknowledge within 3 business days and provide an initial evidence package within 10 business days after a validated claim notice.

5) OSS / third-party code carveouts: Redwood requests a carveout where claims arising solely from open-source components used by Helion within their prompt engineering/custom code are Helion's responsibility.

6) Insurance & offsets: Redwood asks for a reciprocal cooperation on insurance offsets; Redwood will seek contributions from applicable insurance but will not rely on Helion's coverage to limit Redwood's base obligations.

I've attached a redline (Helion_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and an evidence checklist (evidence-checklist.xlsx) that lays out what we can produce. If Helion can accept the cap above and the narrowed evidence request, Sales can push for a commercial concession (see Ben's note).

Can we get Helion's response by EOD Jan 21? If a call helps, Ben and I are available Jan 22 afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu

Redwood Inference

Jasmine,

Appreciate the quick reply and the practical framing. A few immediate points from our side:

- Cap: Helion's procurement team prefers a cap tied to the specific order's annual value but with the option to negotiate higher caps for strategic commitments. The 12-month fee floor is workable if we have a clear definition of what counts as fees.

- Proof-of-origin: We cannot accept a limited evidence set if that prevents us from demonstrating to a third party where the infringing content originated. Helion needs the ability to request more detailed provenance in escalated situations; however, we understand Redwood's operational constraints — so we propose a tiered evidence process: initial package (logs + model hash) per your timeline, and an escalation path where Helion can request additional provenance and Redwood will provide commercially reasonable assistance subject to confidentiality/OTA limits.

- OSS carveouts: Helion will accept a narrow carveout for customer-supplied code. We cannot accept a broad OSS carveout that shifts risk when Redwood's model includes or was trained on an OSS component that directly causes infringement.

- Insurance offset & subrogation: Helion requests that Redwood's indemnity be reduced by recoveries from Redwood's insurers where applicable. We will accept a provision that allows Redwood to pursue insurance but not to rely on Helion's policies to reduce Redwood's base responsibility.

I've attached Helion's counter-redline (see attached; sent separately by our counsel) with suggested language around escalation and evidence scope. If Redwood can commit to the 10-business-day initial package + an agreed escalation path for provenance, I think we can bridge cap language on the commercial side.

Let's set a call Jan 22 10am PST to go through the escalation language.

Regards,
Lara
Lara Cohen

Lara,

Thanks for the thoughtful note. Quick legal clarifications and a tighter proposal from our side so we have precise contract text to negotiate on the call: 

- "Initial evidence package" will be limited to (i) request/response logs for the time window specified in the notice, (ii) model identifier and deployment manifest, (iii) configuration and prompt template versions. We cannot provide raw training datasets or broad dataset exports; instead, we can provide training-source metadata (source names, not dataset dumps) and attestations about training processes.

- "Escalation provenance" step: Redwood will cooperate to provide additional provenance only when Helion has provided a prima facie showing (a short affidavit) that the initial package is insufficient to evaluate the claim. If escalation requires extraordinary operational effort (e.g., full retrace of training lineage beyond metadata), the parties will meet to allocate costs or use a neutral third-party reviewer under an NDA.

- Cap wording: We propose the following: "Redwood's aggregate indemnity liability for covered IP claims arising out of this Order Form shall not exceed the greater of (i) twelve (12) months of fees paid under the Order Form, or (ii) the direct damages awarded by a court." This keeps the cap commercially meaningful.

- OSS carveout: We can accept a carveout limited to customer-supplied code and clearly-identified third-party code that Helion integrated into its system. We cannot accept a wholesale carveout for open-source used in model development.

If Helion accepts the initial evidence timeline (ack within 3 business days, package within 10 business days) and the escalation path above, we'll mark the MSA redline with the cap language and send a clean Order Form for signature so Sales can close. Ben: any commercial sweetener you're comfortable offering if Helion takes the defend-then-settle approach?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Ops, Contracts
Redwood Inference
